hypothesis_or_artifact: H1 (H-ETF) — the Section 0 closure and the disarming of all collectors
label: DERIVED
claim_quote: **DEGRADED and BLOCKED differ in label and not in operational consequence here.**
evidence_summary: The registered decision function, committed at A.0 before any network call and pinned by test, makes exactly this distinction operational: Section0Gate carries a collectors_armed bool (section0.py:49); every BLOCKED return sets it False (:110, :122, :134) and the DEGRADED return sets it True (:182), as does GO (:149). The registration says the same in words (REGISTRATION.md:41 'Collection proceeds.' vs :51 'Nothing armed beyond the census.') and two A.0 tests assert the two branches differently (test_section0.py:61, :75). Neither measured input fires a BLOCKED trigger: E1 at the published magnitude at the achievable count is 0.6105 (n = 163) against the registered 0.50 floor (floor at REGISTRATION.md:47-48, measured value at :851; power.json:62, :64), and the unstable-as-printed share is 0 of 11 (retro_revision.json:3 comparable_days=11, :9 revised_days=0) against a 0.50 majority trigger (section0.py:25, :113). The third BLOCKED trigger, observability FAIL, turns on the one leg that was never measured, and the registration says so: 'The remaining choice between DEGRADED and BLOCKED turns on exactly one unmeasured input' (REGISTRATION.md:873-874) and 'That measurement does not exist and is not synthesized.' (:883). The claim is therefore not that the function returns DEGRADED — it cannot be fired, because fire_observability raises ValueError on revision_days = 0 (observability.py:49-55, called at :66-67) and the only substitute, the retro n = 11, is barred from promotion (REGISTRATION.md:889-895, :1151-1153) — but that the two branches carry different operational consequences whichever way the unmeasured leg would have gone, while the repository adopted the BLOCKED collection state (REGISTRATION.md:1157-1158) with no BLOCKED trigger fired. The A.0 test fixture for the residual band (e1_reg=0.20, e2_reg=0.15, e1_pub=0.62, e2_pub=0.40, test_section0.py:87) is the map's own worked example of the measured case (0.2015 / 0.1700 / 0.6105 / 0.5225). fire_section0 has no caller outside tests/test_section0.py.
recomputation: Reproduced the power inputs independently with numpy/scipy at the registered model (Gaussian copula, rho_p = 2 sin(pi rho_s / 6), src/etf/power.py:47-55; permutation critical value :70-83) at alpha_adj = 1 - 0.95^(1/2) = 0.0253205655 (src/etf/config.py:25). E1 at n = 163, rho = 0.18: 0.638 (3,000 sims) against the repository's 0.6105 (2,000 sims, SE ~ 0.011) — same side of the 0.50 floor by a wide margin. E1 at n = 163, rho = 0.09: 0.209 vs 0.2015. would_resolve: An amendment stating that the operator closure deliberately took the BLOCKED collection consequence without the BLOCKED trigger firing, and why that is not the 'fitting the rule to the sample' the registration exists to prevent. hypothesis_or_artifact: H1 — ADR-019's rejection of the deadline extension
label: READ
claim_quote: *Amending the deadline to 2027-12-31 and continuing*: legitimate, outcome-blind, and nearly free in compute, and it was declined on what it purchases rather than on what it costs. An extension buys the **published 0.18** assumption only; at the **registered 0.09** assumption the minimum N exceeds 1,200, which at 20.8 admissible days per month arrives around 2031. A Stage B under the extension answers only whether the effect persists at its published magnitude, and a FAIL still cannot separate decay from absence, which is the distinction the registered assumption exists to draw.
evidence_summary: The reason ADR-019 gives for declining is the registered DEGRADED scope, verbatim (REGISTRATION.md:44-46; frozen in code as DEGRADED_SCOPE, section0.py:55-58). The registration pre-committed to that scope as its expected outcome and as an acceptable one: 'The Section 9 arithmetic and the decay evidence of Section 14 point to DEGRADED' (:74-75) and 'A DEGRADED here narrows a question rather than abandoning it, and a BLOCKED is a documented answer, not a failure of process' (:82-85), both stated before the census existed. The registered rationale for the 0.09 assumption (:347-356) is not disputed: :355-356 gives a substantive reason to distrust the undecayed figure ('Registering at the undecayed figure would register an assumption the pre-existing evidence already contradicts'), and that is the ground ADR-019 leans on. The unreconciled point is narrower and survives it: Section 0 registered the published-magnitude scope as this design's expected and acceptable deliverable before any data existed, and GO -- the only place 0.09 is a bar -- had already been eliminated on archive density (:863-867), so what ADR-019 declines is the registration's own pre-registered outcome. The declined option cost zero dollars and ~33 requests/day (:1084-1085) against a 200/day registered flow cap (config.py:136) and a 220-request lifetime total (:1160).
recomputation: [from stored data and code] Using the repository's own projection arithmetic (scripts/power_gate.py:71,78-80: forward days = weekdays x printed_day_rate 333/336, added to achieved 11), I reproduced its published scenarios exactly — 88 by 2026-12-31, 152 forward-only and 163 all-cohorts by 2027-03-31 (matching power.json:116 for 163, :117 for 152 and :118 for 88) — and extended them: N = 237 (E1's minimum, the figure the closure is explicitly stated against, REGISTRATION.md:1015) is reached 2027-07-14, and N = 300 on 2027-10-12. would_resolve: An amendment reconciling ADR-019's grounds for rejection with Section 0's registered expectation and DEGRADED scope — i.e. stating whether a published-magnitude answer was, or was not, the answer this registration set out to buy.
confidence_why: Both texts are in the same repository, one rejects the scope the other registered in advance as its expected outcome, and the registered expectation predates any data.

hypothesis_or_artifact: H1 — reopen path (a), and the revision-integrity measurement dropped at Amendment 6
label: READ
claim_quote: **(a)** A flow source serving a **per-row publication timestamp**. Measured: **0 of 2** surviving sources serve one, and none documents a publication time. This removes the dependence on this repository's own capture cadence entirely and would make the full **333-day** out-of-sample series admissible in a single pass, clearing every minimum on the record at once.
evidence_summary: A per-row publication timestamp establishes when a row was published, not what value stood at that time, and the registered admissibility rule turns on the second: the as-printed value is 'the one in that capture' and a later value 'is never substituted' (REGISTRATION.md:155-158; ADR-002, DECISIONS.md:57-61). Reading today's value for a past row, with a timestamp attesting the row's age, is exactly that substitution unless the source's revision rate is known to leave sign and threshold intact. That revision rate is the measurement Amendment 6 dropped (REGISTRATION.md:1141, :1149), and the same amendment bars the only substitute: a future flow hypothesis 'must measure it from scratch and may not cite the n = 11 figure as evidence of anything' (:1151-1153; in the same terms at DECISIONS.md:607-611). So reopen (a), described as clearing 'every minimum on the record at once', cannot be exercised without redoing from scratch the 15-trading-day measurement the closure declined to finish, while the closure's own valuation table records path (a) as 'Does not need etf-snap' (:1125) — true of the collector, false of the measurement. The retro corroboration that would have carried the point is 0 revised / 0 sign flips / 0 threshold crosses on n = 11 against a registered minimum of 30 (retro_revision.json:3,:7-9; config.py:187) and is correctly refused as evidence (:889-895).
would_resolve: Restate reopen (a) as a conjunction — a per-row publication timestamp AND a revision-integrity measurement at the registered n >= 30 — or record that (a) implicitly assumes the revision rate the repository chose not to measure.
confidence_why: A source serving both a publication timestamp and an as-printed value history would satisfy (a) as written, but no such source is named and the two surviving sources serve neither (docs/ACCESS.md:104, :169).
invalidation_note: Amendment 6 is the final amendment and 4d11002 is the final commit.
disclosure_ref: Partly -- the substance of the dependency is disclosed, which caps this finding at S3. The very lines this finding cites as its evidence are the authors stating that any future flow hypothesis owes the revision-integrity measurement from scratch and may not lean on n = 11: ETFExperiment/REGISTRATION.md:1151-1153 ('Any future flow hypothesis in this house must measure it from scratch and may not cite the n = 11 figure as evidence of anything.') and ETFExperiment/DECISIONS.md:607-611 ('may not be cited by any future hypothesis as evidence of source stability. That measurement must be made from scratch.'), with the refusal to promote the retro figure at ETFExperiment/REGISTRATION.md:889-895 and the same statement at ETFExperiment/progress.md:596-599. What is NOT disclosed, and is all the finding now claims, is narrower: reopen (a) is presented at ETFExperiment/HYPOTHESES.md:84 as 'clearing every minimum on the record at once' and the from-scratch requirement is never carried across to it, so the two statements are never joined.
